first.rationale: The concurrent declines in onboarding completion and activation make onboarding friction the most direct, evidence-backed constraint on durable qualified revenue. Prior onboarding shortening and signup simplification both improved early adoption. I will verify the onboarding result and compare it against promotional pricing evidence before committing, since competitor pricing creates a credible competing urgency but may be less durable.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying the self-serve onboarding flow. The verified prior result directly addresses the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and demonstrated completion +13%, 2.1 fewer days to value, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue rather than only top-of-funnel growth. Signup simplification also previously produced durable SMB activation gains. Do not use aggressive promotional pricing: its verified acquisition and qualified-revenue lift came with 30-day retention down 12% and failure to survive the first renewal cycle. The current activation decline may have additional causes, so measure completion, time-to-value, first meaningful action, qualified conversion, and early retention by SMB segment.
